scale: ARCH candidate for Union-level supervision of general-purpose AI models (SC for Union-level supervision, codes of practice and the fines on those providers)
value_statement: Supervision and enforcement of the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models are stated as exclusive powers of the Commission (implemented through the AI Office), with no national supervisory competence stated in W other than cooperation and requests
inference_rule: Article 88(1) (exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V) combined with the absence statement CL-03 over the declared corpus
aggregation_rule: No aggregation: the value is stated for the single bearer; values per SC were examined first (SC for Union-level supervision)
rival_partition: Treat the AI Office powers over systems of the same provider (Article 75) as national-level market surveillance powers

scale: ARCH candidate for national market surveillance with Union review (SC for national market surveillance, operator duties, incident reporting)
value_statement: Evaluation and corrective measures sit at Member State level with market surveillance authorities; the Commission decides on the justification of national measures and its decision binds all Member States, with no general power of direction over market surveillance authorities stated in W
inference_rule: Articles 79(1)-(9), 81(1)-(2) and 46(5)-(6) for the two levels and the absence statement CL-06 over the declared corpus
aggregation_rule: No aggregation: whole-level statement from the stated relations of the national and Union levels; values per SC examined first
rival_partition: Treat Articles 81 and 82 (Union safeguard procedures) as a separate architecture from Articles 79 and 80

scale: SC for national market surveillance of AI systems with Union review
value_statement: Decision centres are the market surveillance authority of each Member State (at least one per Member State under Article 70(1), a stated multiplicity of one or more per Member State) and the Commission; the number of Member States and so of authorities is not stated in W
inference_rule: Article 70(1) obligation to establish or designate at least one market surveillance authority per Member State; Article 81 for the Commission decision
aggregation_rule: No aggregation across Member States; count-dependent property
count_basis: Stated legal multiplicity: at least one market surveillance authority per Member State (Article 70(1)); the number of Member States is not evidenced in W, so the total number is undetermined
rival_partition: Count the Commission and the Member State authorities as one decision centre

scale: SC for national market surveillance of AI systems with Union review, reported by function
value_statement: Evaluation of the AI system: market surveillance authority (Article 79(2)); requirement of corrective action: market surveillance authority (Article 79(2) second subparagraph); objection to a national measure: market surveillance authority of another Member State or the Commission (Article 81(1)); decision on justification: Commission (Article 81(1)); execution of restrictive measures or withdrawal: Member States (Article 81(2))
inference_rule: Allocation read from the origin positions of the member relations by function
aggregation_rule: Values by function reported first; no summary across functions
rival_partition: Allocate the corrective-action requirement to the operator position instead of the authority

scale: SC for national market surveillance of AI systems with Union review, by function and position
value_statement: The market surveillance authority prescribes the period for corrective action within a cap (15 working days or as provided in sectoral legislation) and chooses among appropriate provisional measures; the Commission decides whether a national measure is justified within stated periods; Member States have no stated discretion once the Commission decision is taken
inference_rule: Discretion attributes recorded on the member relations (Article 79(2), 79(5), 81(1)-(2))
aggregation_rule: Qualitative by function and position; no score
rival_partition: Attribute discretion only to the Commission

scale: ARCH candidate for Union-level supervision of general-purpose AI models
value_statement: The duties of providers to supply information and access (Articles 91-92) combine questioning, assessment and consequences (fines, Article 101) and are classified ACCOUNTABILITY (derived) with sufficiency indeterminate because an explicit duty to justify is not stated; judicial review of fines lies with the Court of Justice (Article 101(5)); the alternative-means demonstration (Articles 53(4), 55(2)) and the code participant reporting remain ANSWERABILITY
inference_rule: Classification of the member relations under RGAM-DR-17 with the derivation stated in the relations
aggregation_rule: No aggregation: classes are reported per relation
rival_partition: Treat all information duties as INFO only

scale: SC for third-party conformity assessment and certification
value_statement: Certification is performed by notified bodies established under national law with legal personality, independent of providers (Articles 31(1), 31(4)); whether a given notified body is a public or a private entity is not stated in W
inference_rule: Article 31(1) and (4) state legal form and independence without a public or private qualifier
rival_partition: Treat notified bodies as private actors performing delegated public functions

scale: SC for codes of practice and codes of conduct
value_statement: Codes of practice are facilitated by the AI Office and the Board, joined by invited providers, monitored by the AI Office and the Board and may be approved by Commission implementing act; codes of conduct may be drawn up by providers, deployers or their organisations; autonomy of providers is bounded by Commission approval and monitoring for codes of practice
aggregation_rule: Values reported for codes of practice and codes of conduct separately; no summary
rival_partition: Treat codes of practice as a delegated rule-making device of the Commission

scale: SC for third-party conformity assessment and certification, Annex III high-risk AI systems only
value_statement: The notified body route is not a necessary stage for Annex III systems: internal control (Annex VI) is the stated route for points 2 to 8 and an alternative for point 1 where standards or common specifications were applied; the Annex VII route is mandatory in the stated circumstances
inference_rule: Article 43(1)-(2) and the absence statement CL-04
aggregation_rule: No aggregation: stated for the Annex III scale only
rival_partition: Treat the notified body as a necessary stage for all high-risk AI systems

scale: SC for third-party conformity assessment and certification, high-risk AI systems covered by Annex I Section A legislation
value_statement: Whether the notified body is a necessary stage for these systems is not determinable within W: Article 43(3) refers to the procedure of the sectoral acts and the scope rests on the legislation listed in Annex I
inference_rule: Article 43(3) and Article 6(1) with the absence statement CL-05
rival_partition: Treat Article 43(3) as incorporating the sectoral requirement of a notified body

scale: Position of the market surveillance authority within SC for third-party conformity assessment and certification
value_statement: For high-risk AI systems intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9) acts as notified body in the Annex VII procedure, so that the notified body role is substituted by the authority in that case
inference_rule: Article 43(1) third subparagraph (conditional attribution of the notified body function)
aggregation_rule: No aggregation: positional property stated for the case in which the authority acts as notified body
rival_partition: Treat the authority as an additional notified body

scale: SC for operators along the value chain of a high-risk AI system
value_statement: Duties towards deployers and authorities are routed through intermediaries in stated cases: the authorised representative stands in for a third-country provider towards authorities (Articles 22, 54), importers and distributors verify and relay information between provider and authorities (Articles 23-24), and deployers inform providers before importers, distributors and authorities (Article 26(5))
inference_rule: Origin and counterpart positions of the member relations by relation type
aggregation_rule: Values by intermediary position reported first; no summary
rival_partition: Treat intermediary relations as bilateral relations with the provider only

scale: ARCH candidate for national market surveillance with Union review
value_statement: Whether the procedure of Articles 79 to 83 is substitutable by another path for AI systems presenting a risk is not determinable within W: Article 74(4) displaces it for AI systems related to Annex I Section A products where sectoral procedures are equivalent, and those procedures and the powers of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 are external
inference_rule: Article 74(4) and the absence statement CL-07
rival_partition: Treat the sectoral procedures as part of the architecture

scale: ARCH candidate for the delegation of power to adopt delegated acts
value_statement: Not attributable: the number of relations from the rule-making position of the Commission to operators cannot be stated because no legal rule links successive relations as steps of a path; delegated acts amend Annex content (objects), not relations
inference_rule: Candidate positional property; path semantics not met
path_semantics: A path step would require a legal rule linking the Commission delegated act competence to a subsequent relation of an operator; no such rule is stated, so reachability is not transmission (RGAM-DR-21)
rival_partition: Count steps by cross-references between Articles
